title: The Fool

seo.title: Destiny matrix 22 — The Fool: meaning of the arcanum
seo.description: The Fool is arcanum 22 in the destiny matrix: freedom, lightness and risk, with the main conflict of the number laid out.

meaning: 22 in the destiny matrix is the energy of the Fool: freedom, lightness and curiosity are stronger than rules. As a number it stands for a person who moves without a ready map and takes uncertainty more easily than others do. One detail of this matrix matters here: the Fool stands not as zero but as the twenty-second, the last one. So this is not a beginner’s naivety but the freedom of someone grown up — the kind that comes only after the other twenty-one lessons have been walked through.

Being the twenty-second arcanum means that every firm rule about how things are done feels like a tight room. Such a person comes alive where there is no instruction and nobody knows how to do it right: where others get lost, they feel the thrill. Inside there is almost always lightness and a readiness for an unexpected turn — and a dislike of anything that cannot be replayed from the start.

The main inner conflict of this number is freedom against escape. The same lightness either lifts the person above what is unnecessary or carries them away at the first hard moment, and from the outside the two look the same. The engine of the arcanum is not a goal but interest: while there is novelty, strength appears by itself; once one day repeats another, the energy drains away. Hence the question their whole life answers: are they choosing freedom or avoiding what is heavy.

In its strong version the twenty-second arcanum is freedom inside what you have taken on, not instead of it: the person stays light but keeps their word and finishes what they started. The weak version is freedom at someone else’s expense, when the lightness rests on the dull part being carried by another. The difference shows in one sign: do they pay for their freedom themselves, or do the people around them quietly pay for it.

What separates the Fool from its neighbour the World is direction. The World is completeness, when everything has come together and settled into place; the twenty-second is the one who leaves that summit again with empty hands, because the finished and the settled feel cramped to him. And what separates him from the Magician, with whom the Fool is confused because of the zero place in the deck, is that he starts with no tools and no plan: he does not turn an idea into a result by effort, he goes on pure curiosity and trust in chance.

article.title: Arcanum 22 in the destiny matrix — The Fool: freedom without a manual
article.short: 22 in the destiny matrix is The Fool, the arcanum of freedom and the blank page. It gives a readiness to get up and go, trust in life and the ability to start from zero where others have neither a plan nor the strength. Its shadow is running away — from decisions, from commitments and from oneself — and the running can be loud or completely quiet. The main question of the twenty-second arcanum is not whether a person is free but what that freedom leaves behind.

seo.title: Destiny matrix 22: The Fool, its strength and its two shadows
seo.description: Destiny matrix 22 is The Fool: freedom without a manual. Its strength and two shadows, freedom vs escape, where 22 sits and where it never appears.

sections.h2: In brief: what 22 means in the destiny matrix

head: Question
Answer

Starting from zero without drama, improvising, seeing the familiar with fresh eyes

In at least one position of the report — for two people in three (66.6%)

paragraphs: If you were looking for the meanings of all twenty-two arcana rather than the twenty-second alone, they are collected in the [encyclopedia of arcana](/encyclopedia/arcanum) — one page for each.

sections.h2: Why The Fool is number 22 when in Tarot he is zero
paragraphs: The Fool is the only major arcanum without a fixed place in the row. On old Marseille cards he has no number at all. Waite gave him the number 0, yet in his book he describes The Fool not at the start of the row but between Judgement and The World. Other systems, as Benebell Wen, author of Holistic Tarot, notes, assign him “22” and place him last, right after The World. The destiny matrix counts the arcana from 1 to 22, and The Fool gets the last number.

Hence the double nature of the twenty-second arcanum. It stands after The World, where the circle is closed and everything is gathered — and at the same time before The Magician, with whom the row begins again. The Fool is what comes after the finale: empty hands once more and the road once more. That is why the energy of 22 sits badly with the words “final” and “forever”: for it, every ending is only the way into the next beginning.

There is also a very down-to-earth sign that this card lives by its own laws. Tarot appeared in fifteenth-century Italy as a deck for a card game, and in France that game is still played. In French tarot The Fool is actually called l’Excuse, “the Excuse”. He has no suit and no rank. He can be played at any moment in place of the card the rules call for: he “excuses” the player from following suit. But The Fool does not take the trick — he neither wins it nor loses it, he simply goes back to his owner.

This is almost a ready-made portrait of 22 in a person. The Fool is allowed what others are not forgiven: to walk in uninvited, to change the rules, to start where everyone else has given up. But freedom on its own wins nothing. Wen puts it briefly: The Fool “is about power, but no product”. The whole lesson of the twenty-second arcanum lies in what that power is put to.

sections.h2: The strength of arcanum 22: what The Fool gives
paragraphs: A person with a strong 22 is not afraid to start over. Moving to another city, a new profession at forty, life after a divorce or a failed business are not a catastrophe for them but a change of scenery. While others mourn the plan that fell through, they are already asking: “All right, so what can we do now?” — and they find a move that stays invisible while your head is full of the loss.

The second gift is a fresh eye. The Fool looks at the familiar as if seeing it for the first time and asks questions that feel awkward to ask among people in the know: “Why are we doing this at all?” Some of those questions really are naive, and some turn out to be the only ones that matter. It is no accident that royal courts kept jesters: a person outside the hierarchy could tell the king what no minister dared to.

The third gift is lightness. It is easy to be around such a person: they don’t hold grudges, don’t keep score, and laugh at themselves before they laugh at others. Their trust in the world looks naive but works: people more often open up to someone who is open.

In Russian fairy tales this arcanum has an exact double — Ivan the Fool, Ivan-durak. His clever brothers calculate everything and end up with nothing. The youngest, in one tale, shares his last crust with an old man and gets a flying ship; in another, he goes to keep watch at his father’s grave in place of his brothers, who cannot be bothered, and gets Sivka-Burka, the magic horse. His luck is not chance but a by-product of not haggling with life. Wen puts The Fool in one row with tricksters from different cultures: Robin Hood, Puck, Kitsune the fox, Sun Wukong the Monkey King. Ivan the Fool belongs to the same family — he is thought stupid right up to the moment it turns out that the rules he ignored did not matter so much after all.
In the plus, 22 is the person you want to call when everything has gone off plan.

sections.h2: The Fool’s two shadows: the loud one and the quiet one
paragraphs: The Fool’s minus is sharp, and Waite described it long ago. In his book he gives the card two lists of divinatory meanings: one for the upright position and one for the reversed. A number in the matrix has no reversed position, but the lists themselves describe with surprising accuracy the two ways in which 22 loses its freedom.

**The loud shadow.** The first list has mania, extravagance, intoxication, delirium, frenzy. This is life at high speed: decisions in a second, money that “came and went”, adventures for the sheer taste of risk, promises sincere in the morning and forgotten by evening. Novelty becomes a habit without which life is dull: as soon as a venture settles into a routine, it is dropped. In the worst version a pull towards anything that switches the head off is added — gambling, thrill-seeking, drink. The word “intoxication” is right there in Waite’s list.

**The quiet shadow.** The second list has negligence, absence, carelessness, apathy, nullity. There is no madness here at all: the person is simply not present in their own life. “Whatever happens”, “I don’t care”, “I’ll sort it out later”. Others make the decisions, the days are all alike, and the only freedom left is the freedom not to choose anything. In the Russian tale this is Yemelya lying on the stove, waiting for everything to get done “at the pike’s command”. Such a person is hard to reproach: they have done nothing wrong. But they have done nothing at all.

Both shadows grow from one root — freedom that is tied to nothing. In the loud version it goes into movement without direction; in the quiet one, into refusing to move. Wen adds a Peter Pan mentality to the portrait: “a willful refusal to take responsibility or be mature”.

paragraphs.h3: How to tell freedom from running away

paragraphs: From the outside they look the same: a person leaves a job, a city, a relationship. Three questions show the difference.

ul: **Am I going towards something or away from something?** Freedom can name where it is heading. Running away only knows where it is coming from.

**What will be left afterwards?** A free step leaves behind work done, experience and people you can still say hello to in the street. Running away leaves things half done and people who now have to clear them up.

**Did something new call, or did I simply reach the middle?** Every undertaking gets dull in the middle. If the urge to drop everything comes at exactly that point, it is not the call of the road but the ordinary middle of the way, and it has to be walked through.

sections.h2: The Fool in the Waite deck: a young man who sees the edge
paragraphs: On Waite’s card, drawn by Pamela Colman Smith, The Fool is a young man in fine clothes who has paused at the brink of a precipice among high mountains. Waite describes him like this: he walks with a light step, “as if earth and its trammels had little power to restrain him”, and he looks not down but into the blue distance — “its expanse of sky rather than the prospect below”. His countenance “is full of intelligence and expectant dream”. In one hand he holds a white rose, in the other a wand from which an embroidered bag hangs over his shoulder. A white dog leaps beside him, and the sun shines behind him. The depth below holds no terror, Waite writes: “it is as if angels were waiting to uphold him, if it came about that he leaped from the height”.

Two phrases from this description are worth remembering. The Fool is “a prince of the other world on his travels through this one”. And the sun behind him “knows whence he came, whither he is going, and how he will return by another path after many days”. Waite fits the conclusion into a single line: he is “the spirit in search of experience”.

The most interesting thing about this card is what Waite changed. In the older designs that he himself recounts, The Fool is looking over his shoulder and does not know he is on the brink of a precipice, while a dog or some other animal attacks him from behind and drives him to his destruction. That is a blind fool. Waite’s Fool sees the edge — and is not afraid. Translated into the language of the matrix, the difference between the two designs is exactly the difference between the minus and the plus of 22: not noticing the danger, or seeing it and still trusting the road. The first is carelessness, the second is freedom.

The bag on the wand has been read in different ways. The version that it holds its owner’s follies and vices Waite called “bourgeois and arbitrary”. He gives no separate meanings to the rose, the dog or the bag: the card is read as a whole. Its number is zero. And the Frenchman Etteilla, who in the eighteenth century published one of the first Tarot decks made specifically for fortune-telling, drew The Fool as a court jester — “with cap, bells and motley garb”.

sections.h2: Where 22 sits in the matrix and what that changes
paragraphs: A number in the matrix is not a label saying “I am The Fool” but an energy standing at a particular point. Freedom at a money point and freedom in a family line are different stories. Below are all the positions where 22 occurs and the share of people who have it there — across all birth dates since 1900.

paragraphs: If 22 stands at several of your points, that is not a “double Fool”. Each position answers its own question and is read separately: freedom in how you rest is a joy, while the same freedom in the karmic task is work for a lifetime.

The twenty-second arcanum is not and cannot be at three points. The spiritual task, point B, holds the month of birth, and there are only twelve months. The decade from 20 to 30 is calculated from the same point, so 22 does not lead it either. At the entry of the relationship line and the karmic tail, point M, the calculation gives only multiples of three — and the same goes for spiritual purpose. If a calculator has shown you 22 at one of these points, the date is worth recalculating.

sections.h2: The talent of 22: where The Fool earns and where he gets bored
paragraphs: When 22 stands on the talent line, it is a talent for starting. A person with it enters the unfamiliar faster than others, does not wait for instructions and is not afraid to look like a beginner. They are good where a task has no ready-made solution yet: inventing a format, launching a project, being the first to go where nobody has been, getting an unfamiliar audience talking, wriggling out when everything has gone wrong.

So the work that suits 22 is where the first step and improvisation are valued, not years of service: launching projects and start-ups, travel and tourism, events and celebrations, the stage, reporting, work with children, scouting new markets. There is even a profession built entirely on the fool’s way of looking — the software tester. Testers earn their living by doing to a program what a “normal user” would never do.

The weak spot of the talent is that same power without a product. The Fool starts brilliantly and loses interest by the middle, when the new has turned into work. There are two ways out: choose short projects where the middle has no time to get boring, or work in tandem with someone who loves finishing things. 22 feels worst in a job where every day is like yesterday and initiative is punished.

sections.h2: Love, money, the centre and the year: in brief, and where to read more
paragraphs: These topics have their own breakdowns on the site; here are the essentials.

**Relationships.** In a couple, 22 chooses lightness: being together has to be funny and easy. The support of such a union is neither passion nor vows but a few firm rules that are kept on any day, not just a good one. In detail — in the breakdown of [22 in relationships](/encyclopedia/position/relations/22).

**Under the heart.** This point shows what a person becomes in closeness. With 22 there, they give their partner a lot of freedom and expect the same in return. The difficulty is constancy: as soon as an agreement is pinned down, they feel the pull to vanish. Gender does not affect the calculation: for a man and for a woman, 22 under the heart is calculated and read the same way. The breakdown — [22 under the heart](/encyclopedia/position/love_middle/22).

**Money.** On the money line, including its middle point, the one called “under the dollar”, 22 brings income through the unusual: your own ventures, risk, anything new. The weak spot is keeping track: money melts away unnoticed, and nobody is to blame. In detail — [the money channel with 22](/encyclopedia/position/money/22).

**Centre.** 22 in the centre of the matrix is rare. Here freedom is not a character trait but what the whole personality rests on: to stay themselves, a person needs the chance to start everything over. The breakdown — [22 in the centre](/encyclopedia/position/center/22).

**Year.** “22 for the year” is a different calculation: not a point in the chart but the energy of a year when the old frames stop holding. About it — [22 for the year in the destiny matrix](/year/22).
5.2% of people have a karmic tail with 22, and it comes in only two variants. Both begin with 3, The Empress.

ul: [The 3-7-22 tail](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/3-7-22) — The Fool at the root of the tail, at the point of the karmic task. If point D holds 22, the tail is always this one. It is called “the Prisoner”: again and again the person breaks free and discovers that the walls have moved along with them. Found in 2.9% of people.

[The 3-22-19 tail](/encyclopedia/karmic-tail/3-22-19) — The Fool in the middle of the tail. It is called “the Unborn Child”: what is begun — a venture, a home, a relationship — is started easily but never comes into the world. Found in 2.2% of people.

paragraphs: There are no other tails with 22: at the entry of the tail, point M, the twenty-second arcanum never appears.

sections.h2: The Fool in a couple’s matrix
paragraphs: A compatibility matrix is calculated from the dates of birth of two people, and 22 in it speaks of the union itself, not of either one. If 22 stands in the personal matrix of one partner, it is about that person, not the couple.

Yuliana Lisovskaya, author of a book on the compatibility matrix, names freedom as the key of the twenty-second energy in a couple. In the plus it is a union of two self-sufficient people who trust each other and so do not check up, take problems and money lightly and calmly start from scratch. In the minus the couple lives like neighbours: the status of the relationship is unclear, and an easy start breaks at the first serious step. What The Fool means at each point of the couple is on a separate page about 22 in compatibility.

sections.h2: How The Fool differs from similar arcana

head: Arcanum
How it resembles The Fool
How it differs
rows: The Magician channels power into a result. The Fool, in Wen’s words, has power but no product yet
The Lovers’ choice is a moral one. The Fool’s is between two forks in the path, one leading to flight and the other to a fall, and maturity decides
The Chariot drives towards a goal and holds its course. The Fool walks for the sake of walking and finds the goal along the way
A wanderer apart from the crowd
The Hermit goes away in order to understand. The Fool, in order to try
The Sun is joy that has found its place and warms others. The Fool is openness still on the road
The World: the circle is closed, everything is gathered. The Fool is what begins afterwards

paragraphs: How 22 behaves next to each of these arcana in one matrix is covered on the combination pages — for example, [The Fool and The Magician](/encyclopedia/combination/1-22) or [The Fool and The World](/encyclopedia/combination/21-22).

sections.h2: How to live 22 in the plus

ol: **Decide when you will leave before you go in.** Before a new venture, set yourself an exit condition: three months, the first income, the first ten clients. Then leaving becomes a decision rather than an escape from boredom.

**Set up a freedom fund.** Freedom costs money. A cushion for a few months of living turns “drop everything” from a step into nowhere into a calm transition, and keeps its price off the shoulders of those close to you.

**Fit the new in, don’t swap everything for it.** The need for novelty does not have to be fed by destruction: a new route, a skill, a trip, a project within the same job. The Fool needs freshness, not a fire.

**Get through one middle.** Pick one venture and take it through the boring middle to the end, even if the interest has died. Knowing once what that feels like is the best antidote to the eternal start.

**Against the quiet shadow — a small choice every day.** If you recognised yourself in “whatever happens”, start with small things: decide for yourself where to go in the evening, what to cook, how to reply. Freedom comes back through choosing, not through leaving.
**Plan the unplanned.** It sounds like a paradox, but a day or an evening a week with no programme does The Fool good. When spontaneity has its own place, it does not need to break everything else.

paragraphs: A mature Fool does not stop being free. It is just that his freedom leaves something behind other than footprints.
